summary: The student has successfully created a Windows Forms Name Display application that meets all core functionality requirements. The application contains a button that, when clicked, displays the student's name "Ben Schoolland" in a label. The code includes appropriate comments and follows basic C# conventions, though there are some minor naming inconsistencies that could be improved.

requirementResults.requirement: Button triggers name display in a label
requirementResults.feedback: The application has a properly implemented button (ShowNameButton) with a Click event handler (btnDisplayName_Click) that successfully sets the label text to display the author's name when clicked.

requirementResults.requirement: Follow C# naming conventions (prefer CamelCase, avoid abbreviations)
requirementResults.feedback: Mixed naming conventions: ShowNameButton follows proper CamelCase, but lblName uses Hungarian notation. The event handler name btnDisplayName_Click also uses abbreviated prefix. Variables use correct camelCase (authorName).
The code is well-commented with comments explaining the constructor initialization, button click functionality, variable creation, and the label text assignment. Comments are clear and descriptive.

issues.message: Control name 'lblName' uses Hungarian notation (lbl prefix) instead of preferred descriptive CamelCase like 'DisplayNameLabel'
issues.suggestion: Rename to 'DisplayNameLabel' for better naming conventions

issues.message: Event handler name 'btnDisplayName_Click' uses abbreviated prefix (btn) instead of descriptive name
issues.suggestion: Rename to 'ShowNameButton_Click' or 'DisplayNameButton_Click' for consistency with the button name

issues.message: Form text is set to 'Form1' which is the default and not descriptive
issues.suggestion: Change to something more descriptive like 'Name Display App'

issues.message: Event handler is correctly connected to the button click event

positives: Successfully implemented all core functionality - button click displays name in label
Well-structured Windows Forms application with proper event handling
Good commenting throughout the code explaining the logic
Proper use of camelCase for local variables (authorName)
Clean separation of designer file and main logic
Application compiles and runs correctly as evidenced by built executable files
